title: Efficacy and tolerability of cenobamate in patients with severe intellectual disability and treatment-resistant epilepsy: a retrospective analysis
summary:
Epilepsy is a common chronic neurological disorder that affects about 1% of the population. However, it occurs significantly more frequently in people with intellectual disabilities and often has a more severe course. A significant proportion of those affected suffer from so-called treatment-resistant epilepsy, in which seizures cannot be adequately controlled despite multiple medications.
The drug cenobamate, approved in 2021, has shown promising results in initial studies, particularly for seizures that are difficult to treat. However, there is currently only limited data on its use in people with intellectual developmental disabilities.
The aim of this study is therefore to investigate the efficacy and tolerability of cenobamate in this patient group in everyday clinical practice. To this end, routine data will be retrospectively analyzed, particularly regarding seizure frequency before and during therapy as well as any side effects that occur. Based on this, practical insights for the future use of the medication will be gained.

interventions.name: A retrospective analysis of 75 patients treated with cenobamate at the Séguin Clinic at the Kehl-Kork Epilepsy Center between 2020 and 2025, focusing on efficacy and tolerability.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All individuals over the age of 18 with treatment-resistant epilepsy who have been treated with cenobamate at the Séguin Clinic to date. Since cenobamate has been approved since 2021, data from the previous year will also be included in the analysis to ensure a comparison between the period before and after the medication was introduced. This results in the inclusion of data from the period between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2025.
Exclusion criteria:
None.
